item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a source showing a nationwide decline in political violence, intergroup violence, or displacement in 2024 that would outweigh the Papua conflict record. The evidence is heavily concentrated in Papua plus the August 2024 election-law protests; I did not find a broad countrywide safety improvement metric for 2024.","evidence":[{"title":"2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Indonesia","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"2025-08-12","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html","summary":"The report says Indonesia saw no significant human-rights improvement in 2024, with credible reports of arbitrary killings, torture, arbitrary detention, serious abuses in Papua, and displacement of thousands by violence between state forces and separatists. This is the strongest broad negative evidence that citizens were not clearly safer than they had been.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7"]},{"title":"2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Indonesia","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"2025-08-12","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html","summary":"The same report also notes some limited accountability, including the army’s apology and detention of 13 soldiers after a torture video surfaced, and some investigations/prosecutions of nongovernmental abuses. This is a narrow positive signal, but it is reactive and does not show a durable reduction in domestic violence.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.4","3B.6"]},{"title":"“If It’s Not Racism, What Is It?”: Discrimination and Other Abuses Against Papuans in Indonesia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-09-18","url":"https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-it-s-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in","summary":"HRW says Indonesian security forces committed arbitrary arrests, torture, extrajudicial killings, and mass forced displacement in Papua, and were seldom held to account. That directly undercuts any claim that 2024 left vulnerable citizens safer.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7"]},{"title":"Annual Overview 2024","publisher":"Papuans Behind Bars","date":"2025-07-23","url":"https://papuansbehindbars.org/annual-overview-2024/","summary":"The group recorded 370 political arrests in 2024; most detainees were released within hours or days, but 18 were prosecuted and the report shows continued coercive pressure rather than a safer political environment.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9"]},{"title":"Annual Report 2024: Human Rights and Conflict in West Papua","publisher":"Human Rights Monitor","date":"2024","url":"https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/annual-report-2024-human-rights-and-conflict-in-west-papua/","summary":"The report says extrajudicial killings reached 18 cases in 2024, torture and ill-treatment reached 53 cases, and indigenous Papuans were the main victims, with the pattern tied to discrimination and impunity.
